data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel is more reliable because it converts the judgment process into a 'Trace-to-Outcome' graph, where reliability is measured by the logical coherence of the path rather than the final answer.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist items are too abstract to allow for a granular evidence trace.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The non-experts are trained to 'back-fill' the evidence trail after they have already decided on the outcome.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reliability is evidenced by the 'path' taken through the checklist. Mere compliance is a 'jump' from start to finish (marking all boxes without verification). Within a single evaluation, the presence of a detailed, evidence-linked audit trail for each checklist item distinguishes a reliable judgment from a lucky guess that happened to track the right answer.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
